calls.reasoning: Anchor is the last published close, 2.76% (2026-09-15), and the 2026 base rate for 12-business-day changes (median -0.02) gives 2.74. The 9/11->9/15 move from 2.65 to 2.76 is a three-session pre-FOMC pop; the two 2026 analogues of a >=0.10 two-day pop in the tight regime (late June, late July) both fully retraced within 12 sessions, while the Feb pop continued wider - so I pull the median only part-way back toward the three-month center of ~2.70 rather than all the way. Dispersion comes from the 2026 empirical 12-day change distribution, not the calmer post-April subsample, because the macro tape is live: ~88% priced for a 25bp Fed HIKE at the decision landing today, Brent >$100, 30y UST 5.35% (highest since 2007), record diesel prices, $14.2bn of three-week US equity-fund outflows. Offsetting: healthy HY fund inflows, a refi-dominated primary calendar, improved index credit quality, and no Oct 1 funding lapse (CR signed 9/2 runs to Dec 11). Net: median 2.74 with a right skew - spreads at 2.76 are near historic tights and have far more room to widen on a shock than to tighten on good news. No human prediction market prices this (Polymarket/Manifold: none found by harness; Kalshi: macro contracts only, no credit-spread market), so no crowd blend. 2% above the open upper bound of 3.505, which requires +0.75 in 12 sessions - roughly 2-3x the fastest pace seen in the March 2026 episode; no mechanism for the lower bound (1.745 is below the series' all-time low), so no p_below_lower declared.
